ml-linreg-origin-01: Model mein intercept nahi hai — line origin se guzarti hai. Isliye centred $S_{xy}/S_{xx}$ wala slope yahan kaam nahi karega.
$\sum (y-wx)^2$ ko $w$ se differentiate karke 0 rakho: $w=\sum xy/\sum x^2$. Yahan $x = 1,2,3,4$ aur $y = 2,3,7,8$.
$\sum x^2 = 1+4+9+16 = 30$. Ab har column ka $x\cdot y$ jod ke $\sum xy$ nikaalo. Trap: $\sum y/\sum x = 20/10$ mat lo — wo least squares nahi hai.
ml-linreg-origin-02: Sirf ek parameter $w$ hai aur koi intercept nahi — toh ek hi equation milegi; centring ($\bar x$, $\bar y$) ka yahan koi role nahi.
Derivative zero karo: $\frac{d}{dw}\sum (y_i - wx_i)^2 = -2\sum x_i(y_i - wx_i) = 0$.
Bracket kholo aur $w$ wale term ko ek taraf le jao, phir $w$ ke liye solve karo. Trap: $\sum y_i/\sum x_i$ sirf $\sum(y_i - wx_i)=0$ solve karta hai — derivative mein $x_i$ ka factor hai.
ml-linreg-origin-03: Model origin se forced hai, aur poocha hai minimum SSE — sirf $w$ nahi. Pehle best $w$, phir squared residuals ka sum.
$w=\sum xy/\sum x^2$, aur shortcut: $SSE_{\min} = \sum y^2 - (\sum xy)^2/\sum x^2$.
$\sum xy = 2+6+36 = 44$, $\sum x^2 = 21$, $\sum y^2 = 94$ — ab shortcut mein daalo. Trap: sirf $(\sum xy)^2/\sum x^2$ pe ruk mat jaana, wo explained part hai.
ml-linreg-origin-04: Intercept nahi hai — toh sirf $w$ ki ek normal equation hai. Har statement ke liye socho: ye isi equation se aata hai ya intercept wali equation se?
$w$ ki condition: $\frac{d}{dw}\sum e_i^2 = -2\sum x_i e_i = 0$. $\sum e_i = 0$ aur $(\bar x,\bar y)$ wali baatein $\partial/\partial a$ se aati hain — kya $a$ is model mein hai?
Doubling ke liye $w=\sum xy/\sum x^2$ mein $x\to 2x$ daalo: numerator mein factor 2, denominator mein kitna? Shak ho toh $x=1,2$, $y=1,1$ pe $\sum e_i$ nikaal ke dekho.
ml-linreg-origin-05: Feature $x$ nahi, $x^2$ hai — model $y = w\phi$ with $\phi = x^2$. Isliye simple $\sum xy/\sum x^2$ nahi chalega.
Through-origin formula feature $\phi$ ke saath: $w = \sum \phi y/\sum \phi^2 = \sum x^2 y/\sum x^4$.
$\phi$ values: $x=1\to 1$, $x=2\to 4$. Numerator ka pehla term $1\cdot 3 = 3$; doosra term aur denominator khud nikaalo. Trap: denominator $\sum\phi^2$ hai, $\sum x^2$ nahi.
ml-linreg-ols-01: Intercept $a$ poocha hai, slope nahi. Pehle slope $b$ chahiye, phir mean point $(\bar x,\bar y)$ se $a$.
$b = S_{xy}/S_{xx}$ (centred sums), phir $a = \bar y - b\bar x$. Yahan $\bar x = 3$, $\bar y = 6$.
Deviations: $x-\bar x = -2,-1,0,1,2$ aur $y-\bar y = -3,-2,0,2,3$; $S_{xx}=10$. Ab $S_{xy}$ aur $b$ nikaalo. Trap: $a=\bar y + b\bar x$ nahi — minus hai.
ml-linreg-ols-02: Simple regression with intercept mein $R^2$ = correlation $r$ ka square. Line fit kiye bina centred sums se seedha nikal jaata hai.
$x-\bar x = -1.5,-0.5,0.5,1.5$ aur $y-\bar y = -2,0,-1,3$; $S_{xx}=5$. Ab $S_{xy}$ aur $S_{yy}$ nikaalo. Trap: $r$ pe ruk mat jaana — $R^2$ uska square hai.
ml-linreg-ols-03: Do parameters ($a$, $b$) hain, toh do partial derivatives zero karne honge — options ko inhi do equations se match karo.
$\partial/\partial a$: $\sum(y_i - a - bx_i)=0$; $\partial/\partial b$: $\sum x_i(y_i - a - bx_i)=0$.
Pehli equation expand karo: constant $a$ ko $n$ points pe jodne se kya milta hai? Trap: doosri equation mein $a$ ke saath $\sum x_i$ aata hai ya $\sum x_i^2$ — dhyan se multiply karo.
ml-linreg-ols-04: Intercept hai — toh $a$ wali normal equation bhi milti hai. Har option ko is equation ya OLS ki orthogonality property se check karo.
$a$ ki equation: $\sum (y_i - a - bx_i) = 0$. Aur fitted values residuals ke orthogonal hote hain: $\sum \hat y_i e_i = 0$ ($y_i$ nahi, $\hat y_i$).
$\sum y_ie_i$ ke liye $y_i = \hat y_i + e_i$ likh ke expand karo — kya bachta hai? $R^2$: kya OLS hamesha kam se kam $\hat y = \bar y$ ($b=0$) jitna achha fit de sakta hai?
ml-linreg-ols-05: Data nahi, sirf sums diye hain — seedha normal equations mein daalna hai, $n=4$ ke saath.
$\sum y = na + b\sum x$ aur $\sum xy = a\sum x + b\sum x^2$, yaani $4a + 10b = 20$ aur $10a + 30b = 65$.
Pehli equation ko 2.5 se multiply karo: $10a + 25b = 50$; ab doosri mein se subtract karke $b$ nikaalo. Trap: $a$ back-substitute karte waqt sign dhyan se, aur $a$/$b$ swap mat karna.
ml-linreg-ols-06: Residual = observed − fitted, point $x=3$ pe. Pehle intercept wali line $\hat y = a + bx$ fit karni hogi.
$b = S_{xy}/S_{xx}$, $a = \bar y - b\bar x$, phir $e = 6 - \hat y(3)$. Yahan $\bar x = 1.5$, $\bar y = 3$.
$x-\bar x = -1.5,-0.5,0.5,1.5$ aur $y-\bar y = -2,-2,1,3$; $S_{xx}=5$. Ab $S_{xy}$, $b$, $a$ nikaalo. Trap: $\hat y - y$ nahi, $y - \hat y$ lena hai.
ml-ridge-01: Penalty $\lambda w^2$ add hui hai aur intercept nahi — 1-D ridge ka closed form lagega, OLS wala nahi.
Derivative 0: $-2\sum x(y-wx) + 2\lambda w = 0 \Rightarrow w = \sum xy/(\sum x^2 + \lambda)$, with $\lambda = 4$.
$\sum x^2 = 1+4+1 = 6$. Ab $\sum xy$ nikaal ke formula mein daalo. Trap: denominator mein $2\lambda$ ya $\lambda^2$ mat likho — dono taraf ka 2 cancel hota hai.
ml-ridge-02: $\lambda$ chhote se bahut bada ho raha hai — model pe restriction badhi ya ghati? Har option ki direction (bias, variance, training error, exact zero) check karo.
Rule: bada $\lambda$ ⇒ weights 0 ki taraf shrink, model simple ⇒ bias ↑, variance ↓. Training error $\lambda = 0$ (OLS) pe sabse kam hota hai.
1-D formula $w=\sum xy/(\sum x^2+\lambda)$ dekho: $\lambda$ kitna bhi bada ho, kya $w$ exactly 0 banta hai? Trap: exact zero / feature selection lasso ($\ell_1$) ki property hai, ridge ki nahi.
ml-ridge-03: Char alag claims hain — formula, invertibility, feature scaling, training error. Har ek ko ridge objective ke gradient aur penalty ke nature se judge karo.
Gradient 0: $-2X^\top(y-Xw)+2\lambda w=0 \Rightarrow (X^\top X+\lambda I)w=X^\top y$. Aur $X^\top X+\lambda I$ ke eigenvalues = $X^\top X$ ke eigenvalues $+\lambda$.

$X^\top X$ PSD hai (eigenvalues $\ge 0$); $+\lambda$ ke baad kya sab positive? Metres→cm karne se us feature ka weight 100 guna chhota hoga — penalty $\lambda w^2$ pe kya asar? Trap: OLS ki scale-invariance ridge pe mat lagao.
ml-ridge-04: $y$ values diye hi nahi — matlab $\lambda$ sirf $x$ pe depend karega. Ratio $w_\lambda/w_0$ lo, $\sum xy$ cancel ho jaayega.
$w_\lambda = \sum xy/(\sum x^2+\lambda)$ aur $w_0 = \sum xy/\sum x^2$, toh $w_\lambda/w_0 = \sum x^2/(\sum x^2+\lambda)$ — ise $1/2$ rakho.
Ratio $1/2$ ka matlab denominator numerator ka double: $\sum x^2+\lambda = 2\sum x^2$. Ab $x=1,2,3$ se $\sum x^2$ nikaalo. Trap: $\sum x$ nahi, squares ka sum chahiye.
ml-ridge-05: $X^\top X$ diagonal hai — toh dono weights alag-alag nikal sakte ho, poora matrix inverse karne ki mehnat nahi.
$w = (X^\top X+\lambda I)^{-1}X^\top y$; diagonal case mein $w_j = (X^\top y)_j/((X^\top X)_{jj}+\lambda)$, with $\lambda=5$.

Pehle $X^\top X + 5I$ likho — har diagonal entry mein 5 jodo, off-diagonal 0 hi rahenge. Phir har $w_j$ nikaalo. Trap: $\lambda^2 = 25$ mat jodo, aur OLS weights ko $1+\lambda$ se divide karna galat shortcut hai.
ml-logistic-01: Do steps: pehle linear score $z = w^\top x + b$, phir sigmoid se probability. Score khud probability nahi hai.
$z = 2 - 2 + 0.5$. Ab $e^{-z}$ nikaalo ($e^{-0.5}\approx 0.607$) aur sigmoid mein daalo. Trap: $e^{+z}$ use mat karo, warna $\sigma(-z)$ mil jaayega.
ml-logistic-02: Probability $p$ di hai aur score $w^\top x + b$ poocha hai — sigmoid ko ulta (invert) karna hai.
Sigmoid ka inverse logit hai: $w^\top x + b = \ln\frac{p}{1-p}$ (log-odds).
Pehle odds nikaalo: $p = 0.8$, $1-p = 0.2$, toh $p/(1-p)$ kitna? Phir uska log. Trap: odds pe ruk mat jaana; $\ln p$ ya $\ln\frac{1-p}{p}$ bhi galat hai.
ml-logistic-03: Threshold 0.5 nahi, 0.8 hai — toh boundary $z=0$ pe nahi, kisi positive $z$ pe hogi. Aur $x_2 = 0$ fix hai.
$\ln(0.8/0.2) = \ln 4 \approx 1.386$. Ab $x_2=0$ rakh ke $3x_1 - 6 \ge 1.386$ solve karo. Trap: $z = 0.8$ mat rakho — threshold probability pe hai, score pe nahi.
ml-logistic-04: Sirf $\sigma(z_0)$ ki value di hai, $z_0$ nahi — matlab derivative ko $\sigma$ ke terms mein hi likhna hai, $z_0$ nikaalne ki zaroorat nahi.
Yahan $\sigma = 0.8$, toh $1-\sigma = 0.2$ — ab dono factors multiply karo. Trap: $\sigma^2$ ya sirf $(1-\sigma)$ mat lo, aur $e^z$ ki tarah 'derivative = khud function' mat samjho.
ml-logistic-05: Har point ka loss alag nikaalo: $y=1$ pe sirf $-\ln\hat p$, $y=0$ pe sirf $-\ln(1-\hat p)$. Total chahiye, average nahi.
A: $-\ln 0.8$; B ($y=0$): $-\ln(1-0.4) = -\ln 0.6$; C: $-\ln 0.5$ — teeno natural log se jodo.
$-\ln 0.8 \approx 0.223$ aur $-\ln 0.5 \approx 0.693$. Ab B ka term nikaal ke teeno jodo. Trap: B ke liye $-\ln 0.4$ nahi — wahan $y=0$ hai.
ml-logistic-06: Char claims: gradient ka form, boundary ka shape, $\hat p$ ka shape, separable data pe weights. Har ek mein $z = w^\top x + b$ aur $\sigma(z)$ ko alag karke socho.
Chain rule: $\partial L/\partial z = \hat p - y$ (kyunki $\sigma' = \sigma(1-\sigma)$ log terms se cancel hota hai), aur $\partial z/\partial w = x$. Threshold 0.5 $\iff z \ge 0$.
$\hat p = \sigma(z)$ hamesha (0,1) mein bounded hai — kya ye $x$ ka linear function ho sakta hai? Separable data pe: $w$ ko $2w$, $10w$ karne se loss ghatta hai ya badhta hai?
ml-knn-01: Query $(0,0)$ aur $k=3$ — sirf 3 sabse nazdeek points vote karenge; na sirf ek nearest, na poora training set.
Origin se squared distance $= x_1^2 + x_2^2$ (square root ki zaroorat nahi, order same rehta hai). Saare 7 points ke liye nikaal ke sort karo.
P1: $1+0 = 1$, P2: $1+1 = 2$, P4: $4+1 = 5$. Baaki P3, P5, P6, P7 khud nikaalo, phir top 3 ki classes gino. Trap: sirf P1 dekh ke decide mat karo — wo $k=1$ hai.
ml-knn-02: Same data, same query — ek baar distances sort kar lo, phir har option ke $k$ ke liye top-$k$ ka vote gino.
Squared distance $x_1^2+x_2^2$ se sort karo; $k$ odd hai aur 2 classes hain, toh tie nahi hoga.
P1 = 1, P2 = 2, P3 = 4, P4 = 5. Ab P5, P6, P7 jod ke poori sorted list banao, phir $k=1,3,5,7$ pe vote gino. Trap: P3 aur P4 (4 vs 5) ka order mat bigaadna.
ml-knn-03: Dono features ki range bilkul alag hai: age ka spread 40, salary ka 80000. Raw Euclidean distance mein kaun sa feature haavi hoga, aur scaling ke baad kya badlega?
Raw: $d^2 = (\Delta\text{age})^2 + (\Delta\text{salary})^2$. Min–max: $x' = (x-\min)/(\max-\min)$, yaani age gap ko 40 se aur salary gap ko 80000 se divide karo.
Query se P: age gap 28, salary gap 10000; Q: age gap 2, salary gap 12000. Ab raw aur scaled dono distances compare karo. Trap: ye maan lena ki scaling se nearest neighbour nahi badalta.
ml-knn-04: Har option $k$ ke effect (bias/variance, training error) ya k-NN ki cost ke baare mein hai — har jagah direction dhyan se check karo.
$k=1$: har training point khud ka nearest hai ⇒ training error 0, jagged boundary (low bias, high variance). $k$ badhao ⇒ zyada neighbours ka average.
$k=n$ pe socho: har query ko kaunsa label milega, aur training error kitna hoga? Cost: k-NN 'training' mein sirf data store karta hai — distances kab compute hote hain?
ml-knn-05: Ye regression hai: 3 nearest points ke $y$ ka mean, vote nahi. Distance sirf $x$ pe hai: $|x - 5|$.
Har $x$ ke liye $|x-5|$ nikaalo, 3 sabse chhote chuno, phir unke $y$ values ka average lo.
$x=4$ ka distance 1, $x=7$ ka 2; teesra nearest $x=2$ (distance 3) hai ya $x=9$ (distance 4)? Phir unke $y$ jodo. Trap: neighbours ke $x$ ka average mat lo, $y$ ka lo.
ml-naive-bayes-01: Prior $P(\text{spam}) = 0.3$ diya hai — spam rare class hai, isliye prior ko score mein multiply karna zaroori hai. Dono classes ke score banake normalise karna hai.
Score(c) $= P(c)\cdot P(W_1{=}1\mid c)\cdot P(W_2{=}1\mid c)$, aur posterior = spam score / (spam + ham score). Yahan $P(\text{ham}) = 0.7$.
Spam score $= 0.3\times0.6\times0.5$. Ab ham score $0.7\times0.2\times0.3$ nikaalo aur normalise karo. Trap: priors chhod ke sirf likelihoods ($0.30$ vs $0.06$) compare karna galat hai.
ml-naive-bayes-02: Do kaam: pehle naive Bayes se dono classes ka posterior, phir 'prediction galat hone ki probability' $= 1 - \max$ posterior.
Score(c) $= P(c)\cdot P(\text{Sunny}\mid c)\cdot P(\text{Weak}\mid c)$, sab table se gin ke (no smoothing). Phir dono scores ke sum se divide karo.
Yes ke 4 rows hain (1, 3, 5, 6): $P(\text{Yes}) = 0.4$, unme Sunny 2 aur Weak 4. Ab No class (6 rows) ke counts gino. Trap: max posterior hi report mat karna, aur priors mat chhodna.
ml-naive-bayes-03: Laplace add-one: har word ke count mein 1 judta hai, toh class ka total bhi badhega — vocabulary mein $V = 10$ words hain.
Numerator $3+1 = 4$. Denominator mein sirf 1 nahi, $V$ judta hai — har word ka +1 total mein aata hai. Ab divide karo. Trap: Bernoulli wala +2 bhi yahan nahi lagta.
ml-naive-bayes-04: 'Naive' assumption features ke beech ki dependence ke baare mein hai — aur wo bhi class pata hone ke baad. Priors ya Gaussian shape ki baat alag models ki hai.
Bayes: $P(y\mid x)\propto P(y)\,P(x_1,\dots,x_d\mid y)$. Naive assumption is joint likelihood ko simple product mein todti hai.
Do options product jaise dikhte hain — ek mein har factor pe condition $\mid y$ hai, ek mein nahi. Trap: marginal independence aur conditional independence (given class) alag cheezein hain.
ml-naive-bayes-05: Char claims: zero counts, priors, duplicate feature, smoothing ka asar. Har ek ko NB score $P(c)\prod_j P(x_j\mid c)$ pe test karo.
Score ek product hai: ek factor 0 ⇒ poora product 0. Har feature apna alag factor deta hai, aur prior Bayes rule ka hissa hai.
Duplicate feature: product mein $P(x_j\mid c)$ kitni baar aayega? Smoothing: count 0→1 aur 500→501 — relative change kis mein bada hai? Trap: imbalanced data mein prior hataana Bayes rule todna hai.
ml-naive-bayes-06: Variances barabar hain par priors nahi (0.8 vs 0.2) — toh threshold means ka midpoint 1 nahi rahega. Kis taraf shift hoga?
$x^2 - (x-2)^2 = 4x - 4$, toh $\ln 0.8 - \ln 0.2 = 2x - 2$. Ab $x$ solve karo (2 se divide mat bhoolna). Trap: bada prior boundary ko $C_2$ ki taraf dhakelta hai, ulta nahi.
ml-lda-01: Fisher direction sirf means ka difference nahi hai — $S_W$ identity nahi hai (off-diagonal 1), isliye correlation ka correction lagega.
$\mu_1-\mu_2 = (-2, 1)$ aur $S_W^{-1} = \frac13\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}$. Ab multiply karo; scale aur sign se direction nahi badalti. Trap: $S_W$ se multiply mat karo, inverse se karo.
ml-lda-02: Sawaal hai boundary linear kyun hai — Gaussian log-density mein $x$ ka quadratic term kab gayab hota hai, wo socho.
$\ln p_k(x)$ mein term $-\frac12 x^\top\Sigma_k^{-1}x$ hota hai. Do classes ke log-ratio mein ye tabhi cancel hoga jab dono ka ye term same ho.

Har option ko is term pe test karo: alag-alag $\Sigma_k$ se kya bachega? Priors sirf constant $\ln\pi_k$ jodte hain. Trap: 'features independent given class' naive Bayes ki assumption hai, LDA ki nahi.
ml-lda-03: Variance same (4) hai par prior $A$ ka bada hai — threshold midpoint 4 se hatega. $A$ zyada likely hai, toh uska region badhega ya ghatega?
$(t-2)^2 - (t-6)^2 = 8t - 32$, toh $\ln 0.75 - \ln 0.25 = t - 4$. Ab $t$ nikaalo. Trap: shift formula mein $\sigma^2 = 4$ lagta hai, $\sigma = 2$ nahi.
ml-lda-04: 'Scatter' ki definition stem mein di hai: $\sum (x-\bar x)^2$, $n$ se divide nahi. Aur numerator mein means ka difference squared hai.
$J = (\bar x_A - \bar x_B)^2/(s_A^2 + s_B^2)$: pehle dono classes ke means, phir har class ka scatter.
$\bar x_A = 2$, $\bar x_B = 7$; class A ke deviations $-1, 0, 1$, toh $s_A^2 = 2$. Ab $s_B^2$ aur $J$ nikaalo. Trap: variance ($s^2/n$) mat lo, aur difference ka square mat bhoolo.
ml-lda-05: Char claims: objective, directions ki ginti, PCA se comparison, unequal covariance. Yaad rakho: LDA labels use karta hai aur class separation dhoondhta hai.
Fisher criterion = between-class separation / within-class spread along $w$. $K$ classes ke liye $S_B$ = $K$ class means ka overall mean ke around scatter.
$K$ vectors $\mu_k - \mu$ ka (weighted) sum zero hota hai — toh $S_B$ ka rank max kitna ho sakta hai? Unequal covariances pe Bayes boundary kaisa banta hai (QDA yaad karo)?
ml-svm-margin-01: Dono margin hyperplanes $w^\top x + b = +1$ aur $-1$ ke beech ki poori doori chahiye — boundary se sirf ek side tak nahi. $b$ ka isme koi role nahi.
Width $= 2/\lVert w\rVert$, jahan $\lVert w\rVert$ Euclidean norm hai: $\sqrt{3^2 + 4^2}$.
Pehle $\lVert w\rVert = \sqrt{9+16}$ nikaalo, phir 2 ko usse divide karo. Trap: $1/\lVert w\rVert$ sirf half-width hai; $\lVert w\rVert^2$ ya $3+4$ se divide mat karo.
ml-svm-margin-02: Hard-margin SVM ka margin opposite classes ke sabse nazdeek points (support vectors) se decide hota hai. Pehle dhoondo kaunsa +1 aur kaunsa −1 point sabse paas hain.
Agar ek hi pair support vectors hai: $w \propto x_+ - x_-$, aur $w^\top x_+ + b = 1$, $w^\top x_- + b = -1$. Width $= 2/\lVert w\rVert$.
Opposite pairs ki doori: A–C $= \sqrt 8$, A–D $= \sqrt{13}$; B wale pairs aur door hain. Ab A, C se $w$ aur $b$ nikaalo. Trap: $1/\lVert w\rVert$ half-width hai, poori width nahi.
ml-svm-margin-03: Support vectors woh points hain jo solution $w$ ko 'pakad' ke rakhte hain — socho kaunse points hata do toh bhi $w$ nahi badlega.
Dual mein $w = \sum_i \alpha_i y_i x_i$; sirf $\alpha_i > 0$ wale points contribute karte hain, aur unke liye $y_i(w^\top x_i+b) = 1$.
Margin se bahut door wala point: uska constraint active hai ya inactive, toh $\alpha_i$ kya hoga? Trap: hard margin mein training pe koi misclassified point hota hi nahi.
ml-svm-margin-04: Margin hyperplane pe hone ka matlab $y\,f(x) = 1$ exactly. Har point ka $y f(x)$ nikaal ke gino — $f(x)=0$ wale points nahi dhoondhne.
$f(x) = x_1 - x_2$ har point pe nikaalo aur label $y$ se multiply karo: $yf = 1$ ⇒ margin pe, $yf > 1$ ⇒ margin ke bahar.
P1: $f = 1$, $yf = 1$ (margin pe); P3: $f = 3$, $yf = 3$ (bahar). Baaki chaar points khud check karo. Trap: har class ka sirf ek support vector maan lena galat hai.
ml-svm-margin-05: Point se hyperplane ki geometric doori chahiye — raw score $w^\top x + b$ ko norm se normalise karna padega.
Score: $|6\cdot3 + 8\cdot4 - 10| = 40$. Ab $\lVert w\rVert = \sqrt{36+64}$ se divide karo. Trap: $\lVert w\rVert^2$ ya $6+8$ se divide mat karna.
ml-svm-margin-06: Char claims: non-support vector hataana, $(w,b)$ ko scale karna, objective ki equivalence, margin width. Har ek ko constraints aur $2/\lVert w\rVert$ se check karo.
Sirf active constraints ($y_i f(x_i) = 1$) solution decide karte hain. Boundary $\{x: w^\top x+b=0\}$ hai; dono margin lines ke beech doori $2/\lVert w\rVert$.
$cw^\top x + cb = 0$ aur $w^\top x + b = 0$ — kya ye same points ka set hai? $2/\lVert w\rVert$ badhana aur $\lVert w\rVert$ ghataana same cheez hai? Trap: half-width vs full width.
ml-svm-soft-01: $C$ slack $\sum\xi_i$ ka weight hai — $C$ badhane se har violation mehenga ho jaata hai. Har option ki direction isi se check karo.
Objective $\frac12\lVert w\rVert^2 + C\sum\xi_i$: bada $C$ ⇒ slack kam karna priority, chahe margin chhota ho jaaye. $C\to\infty$ ⇒ koi slack tolerate nahi.
Hard margin kis limit mein milta hai — $C\to 0$ ya $C\to\infty$? RBF ki width kaunsa parameter set karta hai — $C$ ya $\gamma$? Trap: wider margin chhote $C$ ki pehchaan hai.
ml-svm-soft-02: Objective ke do parts: $\frac12\lVert w\rVert^2$ aur $C$ guna total slack. Har point ka slack (hinge) alag nikaalna hai — sirf violators ginna kaafi nahi.
$f(x) = x_1 + x_2 - 3$, $\xi_i = \max(0, 1 - y_i f(x_i))$, $\frac12\lVert w\rVert^2 = \frac12(1+1)$, aur $C = 2$.
A: $f = 1$, $yf = 1$, $\xi = 0$. C: $f = 1+1.5-3 = -0.5$, $y = +1$, toh $\xi = 1.5$. B aur D khud nikaalo. Trap: $\frac12$ mat chhodo, aur hinge mein '1 −' zaroor rakho.
ml-svm-soft-03: Hinge loss sirf misclassified points pe nahi lagta — sahi side pe hote hue bhi agar $yf < 1$ hai, toh loss hai.
Har point ka loss $= \max(0, 1 - y f(x))$. Pehle $y f$ nikaalo, phir 1 mein se ghatao.
Point 1: $yf = 2$, loss $\max(0, -1) = 0$. Point 2: $yf = (-1)(-0.4) = 0.4$ — ab iska loss aur point 3 khud nikaalo. Trap: $1 - yf$ lena hai, $1 + yf$ nahi.
ml-svm-soft-04: Seedha formula hai — pehle dot product $x^\top z$, phir 1 jodo, phir square. Order dhyan se: 1 bracket ke andar hai.
$x^\top z = 3 + 2 = 5$. Ab $(1 + 5)$ ka square karo. Trap: $1 + 5^2$ ya sirf $5^2$ nahi — 1 bracket ke andar hai.
ml-svm-soft-05: Char claims kernel trick ke baare mein: RBF ka feature space, $\phi$ compute karna, XOR, aur valid kernel ki condition. Har ek ko '$K(x,z) = \phi(x)^\top\phi(z)$' se judge karo.
Kernel trick: training aur prediction mein sirf $K(x_i,x_j)$ chahiye. Valid kernel ⇒ Gram matrix symmetric PSD (Mercer). RBF $= e^{-\gamma\lVert x-z\rVert^2}$.
XOR: $(0,0),(1,1)$ ek class, $(0,1),(1,0)$ doosri — feature $x_1x_2$ in charon pe kya values deta hai? RBF mein $e^{2\gamma x^\top z}$ ki Taylor series kis degree pe rukti hai?
ml-svm-soft-06: RBF ke exponent mein squared distance aata hai, plain distance nahi — aur usse $\gamma = 0.5$ multiply hoga.
$x - z = (-1, 2)$, toh $\lVert x-z\rVert^2 = 1 + 4 = 5$. Ab $e^{-0.5\times 5}$ calculator se nikaalo. Trap: $\sqrt5$ mat use karo, aur minus sign mat khona — value $(0,1]$ mein honi chahiye.
ml-tree-split-01: Entropy poochi hai (Gini nahi), aur log base 2. Pehle class proportions nikaalo: 8 examples mein 6 positive, 2 negative.
$p_- = 0.25$ wala term: $-0.25\log_2 0.25 = 0.25\times 2 = 0.5$. Ab $-0.75\log_2 0.75$ nikaal ke jodo. Trap: natural log mat lo, aur Gini ($1-\sum p^2$) se confuse mat ho.
ml-tree-split-02: Teen classes hain aur Gini poocha hai — har class ki proportion chahiye: counts 3, 3, 4 out of 10.
$0.3^2 = 0.09$ (do baar) aur $0.4^2 = 0.16$. Ab teeno ka sum 1 mein se ghatao. Trap: sirf $\sum p_i^2$ pe ruk mat jaana, aur $1 - \max p$ misclassification error hai, Gini nahi.
ml-tree-split-03: Information gain = parent entropy − children ki size-weighted entropy. Left child pure hai, toh uska contribution aasaan hai.
Gain $= H(\text{parent}) - \frac{4}{10}H(\text{left}) - \frac{6}{10}H(\text{right})$; right child mein 1+ aur 5−.
Parent 5:5 hai toh $H = 1$; left pure toh $H = 0$. Ab $H(1/6) = -\frac16\log_2\frac16 - \frac56\log_2\frac56$ nikaalo aur $6/10$ se weight karo. Trap: dono children ka simple average mat lo.
ml-tree-split-04: Har attribute ($X_1, X_2, X_3$) se split karke children ke +/− counts banao. Parent 4+, 4− hai, toh $H = 1$.
Gain $= 1 - \sum_k \frac{n_k}{8}H(\text{child}_k)$. Kaam ki values: $H(3/4) \approx 0.811$, $H(1/3) \approx 0.918$, $H(1/2) = 1$, pure child ka $H = 0$.
$X_1 = 1$ wale rows 1, 2, 3, 5 ⇒ (3+, 1−); $X_1 = 0$ ⇒ (1+, 3−). Ab $X_2$ aur $X_3$ ke counts khud gino. Trap: misclassification error dekh ke tie maan lena — entropy se compare karo.
ml-tree-split-05: Char claims: entropy ka max, Gini ka max, gain ka sign, many-valued attributes. Binary case mein sab ko $p$ ke function ki tarah socho.
Binary: $H(p) = -p\log_2 p - (1-p)\log_2(1-p)$, Gini $= 1 - p^2 - (1-p)^2 = 2p(1-p)$. Gain = parent − weighted children.
$p = 0.5$ dono formulas mein daal ke max values nikaalo. Entropy concave hai — kya children ka weighted average parent se zyada ho sakta hai? ID jaisa attribute children ko kitna pure banata hai?
ml-tree-split-06: Gini ka decrease = parent Gini − children ka size-weighted Gini. Left child (4 A, 0 B) pure hai.
Parent Gini $= 1 - 0.36 - 0.16 = 0.48$, left $= 0$. Ab right ka Gini nikaal ke 0.6 se multiply karo aur parent se ghatao. Trap: weighted child Gini ko hi decrease mat samjho.
ml-bias-variance-01: Training MSE 40 aur validation 42 — dono lagbhag barabar, par baseline (≈5) se bahut kharab. Gap chhota hai ya error khud bada hai?
Rule: train aur validation dono high, gap chhota ⇒ high bias (underfit). Train low, validation high (bada gap) ⇒ high variance (overfit).
Diagnosis ke baad remedies check karo: zyada data mainly kya ghatata hai — bias ya variance? Regularisation badhane se model simple hota hai ya complex?
ml-bias-variance-02: Noise ka standard deviation diya hai, variance nahi. Aur bias ko bhi square karna hai — teen terms jodne hain.
$\text{bias}^2 = 0.3^2 = 0.09$. Ab $\sigma^2$ nikaalo aur teeno terms jodo. Trap: SD 0.2 seedha mat jodo, uska square lo.
ml-bias-variance-03: $T = 0.5X$ shrunk estimator hai, toh biased hai — MSE = bias² + variance, dono chahiye. $N(\theta, 4)$ mein 4 variance hai.
$E[T] = 0.5\times 4 = 2$, toh bias $= 2 - 4 = -2$. Ab bias² aur $\mathrm{Var}(0.5X)$ nikaal ke jodo. Trap: constant square hoke bahar aata hai ($0.25$, $0.5$ nahi), aur signed bias mat jodo.
ml-bias-variance-04: Har change ke liye poocho: isse model training points ko kam 'follow' karega (smoother, restricted) ya zyada closely?
Variance ghatta hai jab model restricted ya averaged ho (zyada neighbours, stronger shrinkage); badhta hai jab capacity badhe.
Ek-ek karke: tree depth badhane se leaves chhoti hoti hain ya badi? SVM mein bada $C$ slack ko sasta karta hai ya mehenga? Trap: ridge $\lambda$ aur SVM $C$ ki direction ulti hai.
ml-bias-variance-05: Do alag curves hain — training error aur test error. Complexity badhne pe har ek ke saath kya hota hai, aur bias/variance kis direction mein jaate hain?
Rule: complexity ↑ ⇒ bias ↓, variance ↑. Training error sirf fit ki quality dekhta hai; test error ≈ bias² + variance + noise.
Kya zyada degree wala (richer) model training set ko pehle se kharab fit kar sakta hai? Test error mein bias ghat raha, variance badh raha — sum ka shape kaisa hoga? Trap: dono curves swap karna.
ml-cv-01: Har candidate value ke liye poora 5-fold CV chalega, aur end mein ek final refit bhi ginti mein shaamil hai.
Total fits $=$ (candidates) × (folds) + (final refit), yahan 4 candidates aur 5 folds.
Ek candidate ke liye 5 fits (har fold ek baar held-out). Ab 4 candidates ke liye multiply karo aur refit jodo. Trap: $5 + 4$ jodna nahi, multiply karna hai.
ml-cv-02: LOOCV mein har point ek baar held-out hota hai — toh har model ke liye utne fits jitne points. Aur 3 models compare ho rahe hain.
Fits per model $= n = 50$ (har fit $n-1 = 49$ points pe hota hai). Total $=$ models × $n$.
Degree 1 ke liye 50 fits; degree 2 aur 3 ke liye bhi utne hi. Ab total jodo. Trap: fits ki ginti $n-1$ nahi — $n-1$ sirf training set ka size hai.
ml-cv-03: LOOCV: har point ko hata ke baaki points se classify karo — point khud apna neighbour nahi ban sakta. Error rate chahiye, sirf count nahi.
Har $x$ ke liye baaki 5 points mein sabse nazdeek dhoondo; class match na ho toh error. Error rate $=$ errors/6.
$x=1$: nearest $x=2$ (A) — sahi. $x=2$: nearest $x=1$ (A) — sahi. Ab 4, 5, 9, 10 khud check karo. Trap: accuracy aur error rate mein confuse mat ho.
ml-cv-04: Har option ek property ke baare mein hai: randomness, fits ki ginti, bias/variance, training set ka size. LOOCV ko '$n$-fold CV' maan ke check karo.
$k$-fold: $k$ fits, har ek $(k-1)n/k$ points pe. LOOCV ($k = n$): $n$ fits, har ek $n-1$ points pe, aur ek point chhodne ka sirf ek hi tareeka.
10-fold mein fits 10 hain ya $n/10$? $k$ badhane pe $(k-1)n/k$ badhta hai ya ghatta? LOOCV ke training sets lagbhag identical hain — estimate ke variance pe iska kya asar?
ml-cv-05: Model training targets ka mean predict karta hai — LOOCV mein held-out point mean se bahar rahega, toh har fold ka mean alag hoga.
Har $i$ ke liye: prediction $=$ baaki 3 targets ka mean, error $= y_i -$ prediction. LOOCV MSE = chaaron squared errors ka average.
2 hatao: mean $(4+6+8)/3 = 6$, error $-4$. 4 hatao: mean $16/3$, error $-4/3$. Ab 6 aur 8 ke liye karo, phir squares ka average. Trap: overall mean 5 sab pe mat lagao.
ml-leakage-01: Mean aur SD bhi data se 'learn' hote hain — sawaal hai ye kis data se aayein taaki held-out fold sach mein unseen rahe.
Rule: data se fit hone wali har preprocessing sirf training folds pe fit karo; held-out fold pe usi ko sirf apply (transform) karo, naya fit nahi.
Har option se poocho: kya held-out fold ki values scaler ke mean/SD mein ghus gayi? Trap: k-NN scale-invariant nahi hai — distance bade-range wala feature dominate karta hai.
ml-leakage-02: Har procedure ke liye poocho: kya evaluation data (held-out labels, future days, outcome ke baad ki info) training ya feature choice mein kahin use hua?
Leak-free rule: feature selection/tuning sirf training folds ke andar; features prediction time pe available hone chahiye; time series mein train past pe, test future pe.

Ek-ek karke: full data pe label-correlation se features chunte waqt held-out labels dikhe? *refund_issued* complaint se pehle record hota hai ya baad? Random folds mein training days test days ke baad ke ho sakte hain?
ml-leakage-03: Ek patient ke 5 scans lagbhag same hote hain. Random shuffle mein kya ek patient ke scans training aur validation dono mein pahunch jaate hain?
Rule: related rows (same patient) ho toh group-wise split karo — evaluation deployment jaisa ho, jahan har patient naya hai.

Har option pe socho: kya ye change ek patient ke scans ko training aur validation mein bantne se rokta hai? Trap: stratification sirf class balance theek karti hai; LOOCV over scans leak aur badhata hai.
ml-leakage-04: Har $t$ ke liye ek model train hota hai — toh models ki ginti = $t$ ki kitni values hain. Training window ka size nahi poocha.
$t = a, a+1, \dots, b$ mein values ki ginti $= b - a + 1$; yahan $a = 60$, $b = 99$.
Chhota check: $t = 60, 61, 62$ mein 3 values hain, jabki $62 - 60 = 2$ — isliye +1 zaroori hai. Ab 60 se 99 pe lagao. Trap: ek endpoint chhod dena.
ml-leakage-05: CV mein 99% aur deployment mein 61%, jabki distribution same hai — itna bada gap batata hai ki CV score khud inflate hua tha.
Rule: theek se kiya CV lagbhag unbiased hota hai. CV high aur real low (bina shift) ⇒ training mein koi information thi jo prediction time pe nahi milti.
Har option check karo: high bias hota toh CV accuracy kaisi hoti? Kam folds CV ko wildly optimistic banaate hain ya thoda pessimistic? Trap: 'CV hamesha itna optimistic hota hai' — galat.
